title: VideoExplorer: Advancing Long-Horizon Video Understanding via Hierarchical Orchestration

problem.claim: Long-video understanding requires handling high-branching, multi-granularity decisions and long-horizon reasoning.

gap.claim: Existing agentic frameworks are limited by ineffective control from monolithic agents and inefficient supervision from sparse outcome-based feedback.

contributions.claim: VideoExplorer uses hierarchical orchestration with a planning agent and specialized sub-agents for fine-grained reasoning.
Trajectory level Direct Preference Optimization (TDPO) aligns entire planning trajectories, including evidence routing and termination decisions, with end-task success.
The work creates fine-grained supervision data through teacher-guided, difficulty-adaptive sampling to support TDPO.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present VideoExplorer, its hierarchically orchestrated framework, and TDPO as novel contributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on MLVU, LVBench, and MH-NIAH reportedly show that VideoExplorer consistently outperforms monolithic baselines in accuracy and efficiency.
The authors report that the experiments validate structured control and trajectory-level optimization for long-video reasoning.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies ineffective control and inefficient supervision as limitations of current long-video understanding agents.
VideoExplorer addresses control complexity through hierarchical orchestration involving a planning agent and specialized sub-agents.
TDPO addresses supervision inefficiency by optimizing complete planning trajectories rather than single-turn responses.
Teacher-guided, difficulty-adaptive sampling provides fine-grained supervision data for TDPO.
The authors report improved accuracy and efficiency over monolithic baselines across three benchmarks and provide code through a repository.

source_observation.claim: Separating high-level planning from specialized fine-grained execution can reduce the complexity of long-horizon reasoning.

interpretation.claim: Hierarchical agent decomposition may improve control when tasks require multiple granularities of reasoning.

application.claim: Use a planner with specialized execution agents for complex, branching video-understanding workflows.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether hierarchical orchestration helps outside the evaluated long-video settings.

source_observation.claim: Optimizing evidence routing and termination decisions as part of the full trajectory is reported to mitigate premature commitment and compounding errors.

interpretation.claim: End-task supervision may be more effective when it evaluates intermediate planning decisions as well as final responses.

application.claim: Align multi-step agent trajectories with task-level outcomes when intermediate routing and stopping decisions materially affect results.

exception.claim: The abstract provides no quantitative breakdown isolating the effect of trajectory-level optimization from other components.

unknowns: No quantitative result values, statistical analyses, or per-benchmark breakdowns are provided.
The abstract does not specify model architectures, training configurations, baseline details, or supervision-data size.
The abstract does not report ablations separating hierarchical orchestration, TDPO, and supervision-data effects.
The repository location and code availability details are not specified.
